Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 29 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of PM Narendra Modi’s Visit to Uttarakhand and UP on 14 April 2026 On April 14, 2026, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi visited Uttar Pradesh (UP) and Uttarakhand , where he inaugurated the Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor and reviewed key infrastructure and environmental initiatives. Exam Hints: ✓ What? PM Narendra Modi visited UP and Uttarakhand ✓ When? On April 14, 2026 ✓ Inauguration: 213 km six-lane Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor ✓ Purpose: Aims to improve connectivity and travel time sustainably. ✓ Cost: Rs 12,000 crore ✓ States Covered: Delhi, UP, Uttarakhand ✓ Key Feature: 12 km wildlife elevated corridor. Highlights of the Visit: Review: During the visit, PM Narendra Modi reviewed the Wildlife Corridor on the elevated section of the expressway in Saharanpur, UP. Visit: He visited the Jai Maa Daat Kali Temple in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. Inauguration of Delhi-Dehradun Economic Corridor: Economic Corridor: On April 14, 2026, the 213-kilometre (km), six-lane Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor was inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. Aim: The Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor, developed at a cost of over Rs. 12,000 crore, is designed to cut travel time from over 6 hours to about 2.5 hours while enhancing connectivity, tourism, trade, and economic growth. Connectivity: The corridor connects Delhi with key towns such as Ghaziabad, Baghpat, Baraut, Shamli, Saharanpur (UP), and Dehradun (Uttarakhand), while integrating with major expressways across Delhi, UP, and Uttarakhand. Infrastructure: The project includes 10 interchanges, 3 Railway Over Bridges (ROBs), 4 major bridges, 5 toll plazas, and 12 wayside amenities. Safety Tech: The expressway is equipped with an Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS) for enhanced safety and efficient traffic flow. Wildlife Protection: The corridor features a 12 km wildlife elevated section, among the longest in Asia, 8 animal passages, 2 elephant underpasses, and a 370 metre (m) tunnel near Daat Kali Temple in the Rajaji National Park (Uttarakhand) eco-sensitive zone to reduce human–animal conflict and protect the ecosystem. About Uttar Pradesh (UP): Chief Minister (CM) – Yogi Aditya Nath Governor – Anandiben Patel Capital – Lucknow Wildlife Sanctuary (WLS) – National Chambal Gharial WLS, Kishanpur WLS MoC&I Notifies Rs. 10,000 Crore Startup India FoF 2.0 to Strengthen Deep Tech and Manufacturing Startups In April 2026, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) through the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) notified the establishment of Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (Startup

About Startup India FoF 2.0: Mechanism: Fund-of-funds model building on FFS 1.0 (launched in 2016 under Startup India Action Plan). Objective: The scheme aims to bridge the funding gap for startups by investing in Securities and Exchange Board of India(SEBI)-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which further invest in equity and equity-linked instruments of DPIIT-recognised startups. Timeline: The scheme will operate across the 16th and 17th Finance Commission (FC) cycles. Alignment: The scheme aligns with Viksit Bharat @ 2047, aiming to promote entrepreneurship, innovation, and India’s transition into a global startup powerhouse. Implementation Agency (IA): The SIDBI will serve as the primary IA and a second domestic IA will also be appointed. Operational Flexibilities: The scheme supports AIFs with larger corpuses to meet the needs of capital- intensive sectors like manufacturing. • It accommodates AIFs with longer tenures to cater to startups with extended R&D periods. • The investment multiplier has been moderated to encourage a larger number of AIFs to benefit from the scheme. Structured Segmental Approach: To ensure targeted innovation, the Startup India FoF 2.0 utilizes a segmented approach: • Segment-1 (Deep Tech): Focuses on startups developing novel solutions with long Research and Development (R&D) cycles and high costs. • Segment-2 (Micro Venture Capital (VCs)): Supports smaller AIFs that provide capital to early growth-stage startups. • Segment-3 (Innovative Manufacturing): Targets tech-driven startups in “champion sectors” under the Make in India initiative. • Segment-4 (Agnostic): Supports startups regardless of their specific sector or stage. Governance Mechanism: Selection Process: A Venture Capital Investment Committee (VCIC), comprising industry veterans, will screen the AIFs for selection. Return Mechanism: Distributions (capital and returns) will be deposited back into the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI), after utilizing up to 5% of returns for ecosystem capacity building.

About Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) Launch: The FFS was launched as a key pillar of the Startup India Action Plan on January 16, 2016 by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi to provide long-term capital support to India’s startup ecosystem. Initial Corpus: The Union Cabinet approved an initial corpus of Rs. 10,000 crore, to be deployed across the 14th and 15th Finance Commission cycles. Investment Mechanism FFS provides funding through SEBI-registered AIFs, which invest in startups. AIFs supported under FFS are required to invest at least twice the amount received from the fund into eligible startups. About Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I): Union Minister – Piyush Vedprakash Goyal (Constituency – Mumbai North, Maharashtra) Minister of State (MoS) – Jitin Prasada (Constituency – Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, UP). AP CM N. Chandrababu Naidu Inaugurates India’s 1st Open-Access Amaravati Quantum Reference Facility in Amaravati On 14 April 2026, N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister (CM) of Andhra Pradesh (AP), inaugurated India’s first open-access Amaravati Quantum Reference Facility (AQRF) in Amaravati, AP, on the occasion of World Quantum Day (April 14), marking a major milestone in India’s quantum technology ecosystem. • The facility enables testing and certification of quantum hardware while promoting self-reliance and innovation in India’s quantum ecosystem. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Amaravati Quantum Reference Facility ✓ By whom? CM of AP N. Chandrababu Naidu ✓ Where? Amaravati, AP ✓ When? Occasion of World Quantum Day on April 14, 2026 ✓ Facilities: Amaravati 1S & Amaravati 1Q ✓ Key Feature: Open-access quantum hardware testing ✓ Consortium: TIFR, IISc Bengaluru, DRDO, IIT Bombay ✓ Partners: IIT Madras & IBM ✓ Indigenization: 85% Indigenous Content; part of India’s National Quantum Mission. Dignitaries: The event was attended by R.V. Haraprasad, Director General (DG), Naval Systems & Materials (NSM), Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO); Abhay Karandikar, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST) under Ministry of Science and Technology, MoS&T; and Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India (GoI) and others. About Amaravati Quantum Reference Facility (AQRF): Facilities: The AQRF comprises Amaravati 1S at SRM University, Neerukonda, (AP) and Amaravati 1Q at Medha Towers, Gannavaram (AP), serving academic and industry-focused quantum applications respectively. Features: It provides open access to researchers, startups, and industries, enabling testing of processors, cryogenic systems, amplifiers, and control electronics under real operating conditions. Technology: Operating near minus 273°Celsius (C) (absolute zero) for qubit activation, it represents India’s first indigenous full-stack quantum system with about 85% domestically manufactured components. Consortium: It is developed through a national consortium including Tata Institute of Fundamental

Significance: The initiative reduces dependence on foreign quantum hardware, addresses limited global access, enables certification standards, and positions Amaravati as a global quantum hub. Ecosystem: As part of Amaravati Quantum Valley under India’s National Quantum Mission (NQM), it includes partnerships with Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras, Chennai, Tamil Nadu (TN) and International Business Machines(IBM), with plans for advanced systems like a 133-qubit computer. Vision: The project envisions Amaravati as a “Quantum Valley” alongside other deep-tech hubs such as a space city in Tirupati, a drone hub in Orvakal, and semiconductor and med-tech clusters in Anantapur and Visakhapatnam. About National Quantum Mission (NQM): Approval: The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the National Quantum Mission (NQM), a flagship initiative by the DST under the MoS&T, on 19 April 2023 with a total outlay of Rs. 6003.65 crore for the period 2023–24 to 2030–31. Objective: The mission aims to seed, nurture, and scale scientific and industrial research and development (R&D) while building a vibrant ecosystem in Quantum Technology (QT) and positioning India as a global leader in Quantum Technologies & Applications (QTA). Key Areas: The mission focuses on developing quantum computers (50–1000 qubits), enabling secure quantum communication (Quantum Key Distribution, QKD, satellite links, networks), and advancing quantum technologies such as magnetometers, atomic clocks, and quantum materials. Hubs: Four Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) have been established in Quantum Computing, Quantum Communication, Quantum Sensing & Metrology, and Quantum Materials & Devices at institutions including IISc Bengaluru, Karnataka, IIT Madras, Chennai(TN), IIT Bombay, Mumbai, Maharashtra, and IIT Delhi. Global Quantum Elite: India has become the 7th country to launch a dedicated quantum mission, joining nations such as the United States of America (USA), Austria, Finland, France, Canada, and China. About Andhra Pradesh (AP): Chief Minister (CM)- Nara Chandrababu Naidu Governor – Justice (Retd.) S. Highlights of report: Aim: To create a more efficient, facilitative, and innovation-driven research environment, transitioning from rigid structures toward a flexible, outcome-oriented ecosystem. Source and Coverage: The key findings of the reports are the outcome of an extensive exercise conducted over a period of nearly nine months, involving outreach to more than 400 institutional leaders and insights from over 850 distinguished scientists and researchers across the country. Evaluation: The reports offer a comprehensive assessment of India’s Research and Development (R&D) ecosystem. • These reports outline a series of actionable recommendations focused on enhancing funding mechanisms, institutional governance, regulatory frameworks, and research translation. Key Recommendations: Some of the key recommendations of the reports are: strengthening innovation ecosystems, supporting early-stage researchers, boosting private sector investment in R&D and simplifying regulatory and administrative processes Key Pillars: The reports outline actionable recommendations across four key pillars: funding, governance, regulatory frameworks, and research translation. Key Challenges: The findings of the report highlighted that despite India’s strong scientific talent base, researchers face persistent challenges such as: complex and rigid funding mechanisms, administrative and regulatory obstacles, limited private sector participation, fragmented institutional processes and challenges barriers in translating research into real-world applications About India’s R&D Ecosystem: Global Presence: Indian ranks 38th position in the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025 and emerging as a leader among lower-middle-income economies. Unlike developed nations where private sector participation drives innovation. About IOC 2026: Background: The IOC was launched in 2016 by India Foundation (IF) in association with regional think tanks and institutions. It aims to promote maritime cooperation among nearly 30 participating countries. • The 8th Indian Ocean Conference (IOC 2025) was held in Muscat, Oman in February 2025. Objective: The IOC 2026 aims to bring together key maritime states and stakeholders to strengthen regional cooperation under the framework of Security And Growth for All in the Region (SAGAR). It promotes dialogue among countries, international organisations, policymakers, and academic experts.
